privacyReport.method: Xcode does not expose its Organizer privacy report from the command line, so the report was derived from the archive itself: every PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy in the archive was aggregated (the app's and both SDKs'), and each Mach-O in the app bundle was checked for tracking-permission and advertising-identifier access (otool -L linkage, nm undefined symbols, and API strings).

findings.appManifest: NSPrivacyTracking = true; NSPrivacyTrackingDomains = []; one collected type, DeviceID, purpose ThirdPartyAdvertising, tracking = true, linked = false
findings.googleMobileAdsManifest: declares seven collected types; NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeDeviceID carries tracking = TRUE and linked = true, with purposes ThirdPartyAdvertising, Analytics and DeveloperAdvertising. AdvertisingData, CoarseLocation, ProductInteraction, PerformanceData, CrashData and OtherDiagnosticData are declared with tracking = false.
findings.userMessagingPlatformManifest: three collected types, all AppFunctionality, all tracking = false
findings.appBinary: links /System/Library/Frameworks/AdSupport.framework; carries an undefined external _OBJC_CLASS_$_ASIdentifierManager (from AdSupport); contains the API strings ATTrackingManager, advertisingIdentifier and trackingAuthorizationStatus
findings.attribution: Those references are NOT first-party code. The repository contains no ATT or IDFA reference (the only hit is a comment in AdManager.swift recording the 1.0 removal). The GoogleMobileAds.framework binary in the archive is a 51 KB stub carrying resources and the SDK's privacy manifest; the SDK's 4 MB of code is statically linked into the app executable by the SPM binary target, and it is that code that references AdSupport and the ATT status API.
findings.infoPlist: NSUserTrackingUsageDescription is still present; 50 SKAdNetworkItems; ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = false

d2Decision.gate: Spec section 9.1 and CONTENT-DECISIONS.md D2 permit removing NSUserTrackingUsageDescription and setting NSPrivacyTracking = false ONLY AFTER the archive privacy report confirms that the configured SDK path does not access tracking permission or IDFA.
d2Decision.outcome: NOT CONFIRMED — the manifests were therefore LEFT UNCHANGED and no re-archive was needed.
d2Decision.why: The report shows the opposite of the precondition on two independent signals: (1) the Google Mobile Ads SDK's own privacy manifest, which Apple aggregates into the app's privacy report, declares DeviceID as collected FOR TRACKING; (2) the shipped app binary reaches the IDFA and ATT-status APIs through the statically linked SDK. 'The app never calls requestTrackingAuthorization' is true and important, but it is a statement about our code, not about the configured SDK path, and it is not what the gate asks for.
whatIsNeverthelessTrue: no App Tracking Transparency prompt is ever shown: no first-party code requests authorization, and none appeared in any of the ~15 simulator launches across this task's test runs
every ad request carries npa=1 and rdp=1 with a G maximum ad content rating (EconAdRequestPolicy), so no personalised profile is requested
with authorization never requested, the ATT status stays .notDetermined and iOS returns an all-zero advertising identifier, so no usable IDFA exists
no ad request is made at all on devices set to an EEA country or the United Kingdom (CONTENT-DECISIONS.md D1)

ownerDecisionRequired.status: SUBMISSION BLOCKER — still open, now with evidence instead of an assumption
ownerDecisionRequired.optionA: Ship as archived: NSPrivacyTracking stays true and the ATT usage description stays in Info.plist. Over-declares rather than under-declares, and stays consistent with the SDK's own manifest. Cost: the ASC App Privacy answers must then say Device ID / Advertising Data ARE used for tracking, for an app that never asks permission and never receives an IDFA — an inconsistency App Review may query.
ownerDecisionRequired.optionB: Declare the configuration rather than the SDK's capability: remove NSUserTrackingUsageDescription (which makes an ATT prompt impossible, since iOS requires the key), set NSPrivacyTracking = false, and keep the DeviceID collected type with tracking = false. Accurate for this configuration and matches the ASC answers drafted in metadata.json. Cost: it disagrees with the bundled Google manifest, which Apple's aggregate report will still show as tracking.
ownerDecisionRequired.recommendation: Option B, conditional on Owner ratification, because it describes the binary as configured and removes the only mechanism by which a prompt could ever appear. It is a one-line change in each of two files and needs a re-archive; it was deliberately not taken unilaterally, because the plan's own gate says the report must confirm it first and the report does not.
ownerDecisionRequired.doNotResolveByGuessing: If the Owner wants Option B, re-run this report after the change to confirm the app manifest, and answer ASC from the re-derived state.

buildHostNotes.capacityRule: Every build, test and archive in this task ran through a single-invocation gate: host-capacity-check.sh must pass and no other xcodebuild may be running, retried every 60s. Several runs waited on a Table Talk test run holding the slot.

buildHostNotes.diskIncident: The host started this task below the 8 GiB build floor. Reclaimed space by pruning regenerable caches and 3,772 abandoned scratch directories older than 90 minutes left in the user temp directory by another lane's harness (~11.8 GiB). Worth adding to the disk janitor: it is a live leak, not a one-off.
buildHostNotes.simulatorContention: The 6.9" simulator is shared. A manual screenshot pass was interrupted when another lane launched its own app on it, which is why the screenshots are captured by a UI test that holds the build slot for the duration.
